- name: int_hubspot__contact_lifecycle_metrics
      schema: intermediate
      description: Contact-level lifecycle, email engagement, deal association, and composite engagement scoring
      grain: One row per contact_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_hubspot__contact_merge_adjust (contact_id, email, created_date, first_conversion_date)
      - raw.email_event_data (recipient, type, created)
      - raw.deal_contact_data (contact_id, deal_id)
      - raw.deal_data (deal_id, property_createdate, property_closedate, property_amount)
      business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_hubspot__contact_merge_adjust as the contact universe (one row per contact_id). - Lifecycle metrics: - contact_age_days = whole days from created_date to today. - days_to_conversion = whole days from created_date to first_conversion_date; if never converted, use today. - contact_maturity_segment by age: <30 days = "New Contact"; <90 = "Recent Contact"; <365 = "Established Contact"; otherwise "Mature Contact". - conversion_status = "Converted" if first_conversion_date exists, else "Not Converted". - conversion_velocity_score: if no conversion → 0; else map days-to-first-conversion: ≤1→100; ≤7→80; ≤30→60; ≤90→40; otherwise→20. - Email engagement (left join on email = recipient): - Count events per contact_id: SENT, OPEN, CLICK, BOUNCE (one per matching row); if no matches, counts are 0. - email_open_rate = (OPEN ÷ SENT) × 100 if SENT > 0, else 0; email_click_through_rate = (CLICK ÷ OPEN) × 100 if OPEN > 0, else 0; rates are not rounded or capped and can exceed 100. - last_engagement_date = latest timestamp of OPEN or CLICK events, parsing created from "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"; if no closed deals in that size then 0. - Keep only owners with total_deals > 0. - Compute window metrics across all remaining owners (no partitions): - revenue_rank: position when ordering by total_won_revenue descending (1 = highest; ties break arbitrarily). - win_rate_rank: position when ordering by win_rate_percentage descending (1 = highest; ties break arbitrarily). - deals_won_rank: position when ordering by won_deals descending (1 = highest;
